releaseNotes: V21.1 Hindi Clarity Repair reviews all 1,073 segments in the 85 Original Source dialogues and replaces broken/machine-formatted Hindi with clear natural Standard Hindi suitable for listening practice.
Hindi source segments and Hindi sample/model interpretations were repaired while preserving dialogue IDs, segment IDs, scenario order and critical-detail metadata.
Original Source 82 Document Translation had two truncated legacy English source segments; they were restored from the V18 study-book source and given complete Hindi interpretations.
Original Source 63 segment 07 was corrected from a wrongly labelled romanised-Hindi English segment to Hindi→English.
A small set of obvious English OCR artifacts found during the Hindi audit was corrected (for example 20I7→2017, I.5%→1.5%, and stray OCR characters) without changing meaning.
Service-worker content cache is versioned so the repaired Hindi dialogues are fetched instead of an older cached dialogues.json.
Verified Practice 105-dialogue content, Hindi vocabulary/phrases, Punjabi pilot content, learner progress, My Vocabs, cloud sync and Firebase backends are unchanged.
V21.0.1 adds a multilingual Voice Manager that prefers browser/device voices first, including Google UK English Female and Google हिन्दी when Chrome exposes them.
V21.0.1 isolates the new synthesizeSpeech backend in a separate Node.js 22 Firebase function package, so deploying online voices cannot overwrite the working V20 assessment codebase.
Voice diagnostics now reports the browser/device voices actually available for English and the active language, with Set up voice and Check again actions.
If the active language has no matching browser/device voice, the Voice Manager can use a protected Google Cloud Text-to-Speech fallback and cache generated MP3 audio for reuse.
Punjabi pilot online fallback uses pa-IN-Standard-A; Hindi can fall back to hi-IN-Standard-A only when a matching browser/device voice is unavailable or the learner explicitly selects online voice.

My Vocabs was regression-audited against the approved smart-sheet design. The right-click clipboard section is restored reliably even when the pointer lands on cell padding rather than directly on the input.
No Hindi or Punjabi packaged learning content was changed in this update; the 5-dialogue Punjabi pilot remains a pilot gate before the full 190-dialogue expansion.
V21 pilot adds Punjabi as a separate downloadable language pack without replacing the protected Hindi production pack.
Hindi and Punjabi attempts, completion counts, mistakes, vocabulary progress, My Vocabs and cloud-sync sections are separated by language.
Existing pre-V21 learner records without a language ID remain assigned to Hindi for backward compatibility.
Punjabi uses Gurmukhi content and pa-IN speech/transcription locale; mixed My Synonyms speech remains item-by-item language aware.
The V20.3.2.2 target-language assessment guard is retained for English↔Hindi and extended through the active-pack metadata for English↔Punjabi.
Punjabi pilot contains 5 dialogues (3 Verified Practice + 2 Original Source), 65 core vocabulary records, 65 general vocabulary records, 40 phrases and 96 dialogue-vocabulary records.
Pilot dialogues are excluded from production Mock Test eligibility until full Punjabi editorial and end-to-end QA is complete.
Hindi packaged learning content and the deployed Firebase assessment backend are unchanged in this pilot.
Assessment now validates the required target language separately from semantic meaning transfer.
Limited source-language words, natural borrowed terms, names, numbers and normal code-switching no longer automatically stop semantic assessment; target-language use is reported separately.
Predominantly answering in the source/wrong language now returns Wrong target language / Major correction instead of a misleading excellent result.
Assessment requests now derive the target language from the active language pack rather than hard-coding Hindi, so the same guard supports Punjabi and future language packs.
Cloud-transcription locale selection now follows the active target/source language metadata rather than a Hindi-only branch.
Assessment cache V2 includes source and target language so older cached results cannot be reused across language directions.
The assessAttempt Firebase Function requires redeployment for the new language-compliance output and mixed-language policy.
Practice online semantic assessment now starts only when the learner opens Review for a recorded response; completing a normal practice recording no longer sends an automatic assessment request.
